questions.context: Deniz moved into his flat in March. It is now October, and he is still there. He pays the landlord on the first of every month.
questions.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct form of the verb: Deniz ___ in this flat since March. (live)
questions.explanation: With 'since March', we link a past starting point to now, so we use the present perfect: 'has lived'.

commonWrongAnswers.comment: It's tempting because he still lives there, but 'since' needs a perfect tense.
The simple past suggests he no longer lives there, but he still does.
The present continuous doesn't normally go with 'since March'; you need the present perfect.

questions.context: Last week the agent promised, 'I will send you the flat details tomorrow.' Now Aylin is telling a friend about it.
questions.instruction: Fill in the blank: The agent said she ___ me the flat details the next day.
questions.hint: Think about reporting 'will' in the past.
questions.explanation: In reported speech after 'said', 'will' changes to 'would', so it's 'would send'.

commonWrongAnswers.comment: This is the original word, but after 'said' in the past, 'will' shifts to 'would'.
After 'would' you need the base verb 'send', not a past form.
The present simple doesn't fit a reported promise about the future in the past; use 'would send'.

questions.context: You must to pay the rent before the fifth of every month.
questions.correctAnswer: You must pay the rent before the fifth of every month.
questions.explanation: Modal verbs like 'must' are followed by the base verb without 'to', so it's 'must pay'.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: You must paying the rent before the fifth of every month.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: After a modal you need the base verb, not an -ing form.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: You must to pay the rent before fifth of every month.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: You removed the wrong word; the error is 'to' after 'must', and 'the fifth' should stay.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: You must paid the rent before the fifth of every month.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: A modal takes the base verb, not the past form.

questions.context: My sister lives in a apartment near the university.
questions.correctAnswer: My sister lives in an apartment near the university.
questions.explanation: We use 'an' before a vowel sound, and 'apartment' begins with the vowel sound /ə/, so it's 'an apartment'.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: My sister lives in the apartment near the university.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: This changes the meaning; the sentence introduces the apartment for the first time, so 'an' is needed.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: My sister lives in apartment near the university.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: A singular countable noun like 'apartment' needs an article here.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: My sister lives in an apartment near university.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: You changed 'the university', which was already correct.

questions.context: The tenants asked the landlord to fix the heating. He finally agreed.
questions.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct form of the verb: The landlord agreed ___ the heating this week. (repair)
questions.explanation: The verb 'agree' is followed by a to-infinitive, so it's 'agreed to repair'.

commonWrongAnswers.comment: Many verbs take -ing, but 'agree' takes the to-infinitive.
You need 'to' after 'agree' before the base verb.
After 'to' in this structure, we use the base verb, not -ing.
